name: MLX Audio
description: Local speech generation on Apple silicon (Qwen3-TTS first): scene-by-scene narration from voice profiles, with a manifest and stale-output detection.

install.setup: uv venv --python 3.12 ~/.nexus-local/runtimes/mlx-audio && uv pip install --python ~/.nexus-local/runtimes/mlx-audio/bin/python mlx-audio==0.5.8

python.description: Python in the isolated mlx-audio environment

narrationDir.description: Default output folder for narration jobs (default: ~/.nexus-local/narration)

invocation.summary: Nexus runs worker.py with the environment's Python once per batch: mlx_audio.tts.utils.load_model() then model.generate() per scene. The model is freed when the process exits; downloads are off unless asked for.

io.input: A narration job (contract nexus.narration-job/v1) and a voice profile (nexus.voice-profile/v1)
io.output: <outputDir>/scenes/<sceneId>.wav, narration.wav, and manifest.json (24 kHz mono 16-bit WAV with Qwen3-TTS)

limitations: Only qwen3-tts-1.7b-base is verified on this machine; the other Qwen3-TTS variants are defined but untested here.
Cloning is reference-based (recordings + transcripts at generation time); nothing is trained, and the voice is not fine-tuned.
Delivery instructions and speed aren't available for a cloned voice on Qwen3-TTS Base; requests for them are rejected, not ignored.
Same-seed output was bit-identical within one process on this machine; that is not a cross-version guarantee.
Peak memory is about 10 GB for the 1.7B model with a 29 s reference; don't run it alongside video rendering on a 36 GB machine.
